text:
Aurelia Skyways, Caleb Hassan, Khalil Ali, and Willow attended the Companion Animal Travel Desk staff meeting.

The group reviewed current handling steps for pet cabin bookings and checked that carrier checks stay consistent from desk intake to loading. The team reminded one another to keep language clear with travelers and to confirm each pet's documents before the handoff to the ground team. For Halcyon, the pet cabin holds 64 pets, and that limit must stay part of the standard briefing so no one overbooks the service.

The staff then discussed transfer care between services. They agreed that carriers need careful movement, steady placement, and a final visual check before release. The training point was simple: do not rush the chain of custody, and do not leave any carrier unattended while records are being updated. When travelers ask for reassurance, the desk should explain the process in plain terms and keep the focus on dependable companion travel.

The meeting also covered small service habits that help prevent errors. Everyone agreed to verify names, carrier labels, and destination notes at the same time, rather than in separate passes. The team noted that clear handoffs reduce confusion and help the desk respond calmly if a traveler arrives with extra questions about pet care. The group closed by agreeing to keep the workflow steady and to flag any unusual issue immediately so it can be handled without delay. The meeting ended with the team aligned on the next steps.
